listing.name: Tetrisphere / Blocksphere (djultra64)
listing.summary: Explore Tetrisphere / Blocksphere (djultra64) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Set up a separate upstream copy
steps.instruction: Download the Windows or Linux package from upstream and run the Blocksphere launcher. Select your own Tetrisphere US NTPE revision 0 ROM or ZIP and choose a new, empty folder outside your Portcove library.

steps.title: Carry your progress to a new upstream version
steps.instruction: Install the new version in another empty folder. Copy data/ from your previous Blocksphere installation into the new folder before choosing Play. Keep the previous folder until you verify your settings and progress in the new copy.

managed_acquisition_hold.reason: Blocksphere now uses an upstream installer. Managed Install and Update are on hold while Portcove checks how the new packages handle existing saves and settings.
managed_acquisition_hold.activation_reason: This staged Blocksphere package does not match a reviewed direct-player release. Keep your current installed copy.

presentation.manual_preparation: On first Play, choose your own Tetrisphere US NTPE revision 0 ROM in .z64, .v64, .n64 or ZIP form. The game validates and imports it; no separate installer or BIOS is required. The imported ROM, settings, progress and diagnostics live in data beside tetrisphere.exe. Portcove carries that declared folder between compatible runtime versions, including data present before first Play. Older upstream user-profile data is not silently imported: follow upstream instructions to copy it to data before launching. Runtime rollback carries current data and does not rewind saves. Existing external copies keep their files and runtime update owner. Play has not been tested through Portcove. Linux uses the same adjacent data directory. Keep lib/ beside tetrisphere; the game needs those companion files. A compatible Vulkan driver and upstream system dependencies are required. Play has not been tested through Portcove on Linux.
